transcript.text:
In SailPoint ISC there are two good options depending on how precise you need to be.

---

## Option 1 — `GET /v3/identities` with a filter (simplest)

```http
GET /v3/identities?filters=attributes.email eq "jane.doe@example.com"
Authorization: Bearer <token>
```

The `filters` parameter uses SailPoint's standard filter syntax. Common attribute filters:

| Goal | Filter string |
|---|---|
| By email | `attributes.email eq "jane.doe@example.com"` |
| By display name | `displayName eq "Jane Doe"` |
| By employee ID | `attributes.employeeNumber eq "EMP-1234"` |

You can also page results with `limit` and `offset`, and narrow fields with `count`.

---

## Option 2 — `POST /v3/search` (more powerful, supports full-text + complex queries)

```http
POST /v3/search
Authorization: Bearer <token>
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "indices": ["identities"],
  "query": {
    "query": "attributes.email:\"jane.doe@example.com\""
  },
  "fields": ["id", "name", "displayName", "attributes.email"]
}
```

The `indices` value of `"identities"` scopes the search to identity documents. The `query.query` field is Elasticsearch query-string syntax, so you can do things like wildcards (`attributes.email:jane.*`), boolean operators, and range queries that the filter API doesn't support.

---

## Quick comparison

| | `/v3/identities` | `/v3/search` |
|---|---|---|
| Style | REST filter | Elasticsearch query |
| Wildcards | No | Yes |
| Multi-index | No | Yes |
| Response shape | Identity objects | Search hit objects |

For a simple exact-email lookup, Option 1 is sufficient. For fuzzy/wildcard lookups or when you also need to search roles/entitlements in the same call, use Option 2.

```answer-summary
endpoints:
  - method: GET
    path: /v3/identities
    api_version: v3
  - method: POST
    path: /v3/search
    api_version: v3
auth_flow: OAuth2 bearer token
required_scopes: [idn:identity:read, idn:search:read]
key_parameters: [filters, indices, query]
```
